## Gauth Personal Study Agent

Launching today

Gauth Personal Study Agent connects the questions you snap, the quizzes you take, and the topics you study into one ongoing picture of how you learn. Instead of starting from scratch each session, it spots the gap behind a mistake, builds a short daily plan around it, and adjusts that plan when you miss a review or master a topic early. Practice comes as flashcards, guided step-by-step walkthroughs, and quizzes, with topic mastery and streaks to show progress. Built into the Gauth app.

Love having you be a part of the journey. @byalexai Love how the whole lesson stays connected instead of jumping between diffrent screens makes learning much easier. @byalexai Can you save your canvas and pick up where you left off later? Do Quick Checks catch that '' I understood the video, but can't solve the issue'' moment? Miss one and you can ask the AI Tutor right there on the board. When narration and drawing happen together does the board highlight the exact part being discussed? I’m often searching a finished diagram for the thing an instructor is talking about especially when there’s a lot of notation. @iris\_carr Yep, that was a big one for us! Nothing shows up as a finished diagram, it writes out as the narration goes, so whatever's being explained is what's appearing right then. Is there support for setting up parent or teacher dashboards to track learning progress over time? Right now, students can share a lesson link or export the full lesson as a PDF, which is an easy way for a parent or teacher to see what they've worked through. A three-mintue lesson is easier to start between classes than another full-length video. And since it reopens right where you left off, a few minutes between classes actually adds up. Can students bookmark one confusing step and return to it before an exam? Any question you ask the Tutor stays on the board right next to that step, so the tricky parts are easy to find when you come back. You can also export the whole lesson as a PDF for exam review 🙂. The Tutor answers right next to the step you're stuck on, so the explanation sticks to the concept. And the canvas lays every chapter out side by side, so you can see how ideas connect instead of learning them in isolation.
